display.title: The Secret of the Tailor's Blessings
display.summary_short: For Elul, why we should give each other many brachos, and the story of a sad, poor tailor in Vilna whose blessings always came true, and the Baal Shem Tov who revealed why.
display.summary_long: In Chodesh Elul we wish each other a good and sweet year, and the storyteller explains why we should never tire of giving brachos: a father's parable about someone handing out hundred-dollar bills, and the teaching that every blessing creates angels who plead for us on Rosh Hashanah. Then the story: two students of the Baal Shem Tov visiting the tailors' shul in Vilna notice a very sad man in the corner. The townspeople tell them that his blessings always work, and that Feivel the flax merchant became the richest man in town from them, a secret Feivel let slip when he drank too much at his son's bar mitzvah. The Baal Shem Tov asks to meet the tailor, who tells his life story: he and a partner earned money sewing a wedding gown for a poritz's daughter, and when the poritz offered to free a Jewish family from his dungeon for 300 rubles, the partner refused to help, but he gave all his earnings himself and became a beggar. The Baal Shem Tov explains that this self-sacrifice raised him to the level of the greatest tzaddikim, invites him to live nearby, and he becomes a great student.
display.lesson: Give brachos to others generously, and helping another Jew with self-sacrifice brings great blessing.

advisories.note: A poritz holds a Jewish family in his dungeon for unpaid rent; they are freed.
A drunk poritz is mentioned, and a merchant gets tipsy at his son's bar mitzvah.
The tailor's family lives in poverty and he becomes a beggar.

characters: two students of the Baal Shem Tov

segments.title: The tailor whose blessings came true
segments.summary: The Baal Shem Tov learns that a poor tailor's blessings work because he gave all he had to free a captive family.
